sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento dell'inflazione negli Stati Uniti e delle tensioni geopolitiche in Medio Oriente. Il VIX è sceso a 17.88, ma rimane sopra la soglia di 15. L'S&P 500 ha perso lo 0.16%, mentre il DXY è salito dello 0.18%. Il prezzo del petrolio è sceso dello 0.71%, ma rimane elevato.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to rising US inflation and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. VIX decreased to 17.88 but remains above 15 threshold. S&P 500 lost 0.16%, while DXY rose 0.18%. Oil price dropped 0.71% but remains elevated.

market_impact_summary.it: I mercati azionari sono deboli, con l'S&P 500 che ha perso lo 0.16%. Il settore energetico è sotto pressione a causa della possibile escalation del conflitto in Medio Oriente. Le obbligazioni governative sono in calo, con il TLT che perde lo 0.67%. Il dollaro USA si rafforza, con il DXY che sale dello 0.18%.
market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets are weak, with S&P 500 down 0.16%. Energy sector is under pressure due to potential escalation of Middle East conflict. Government bonds are declining, with TLT down 0.67%. US dollar strengthens, with DXY up 0.18%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.84%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.67%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo dello 0.16%, il VIX è sceso dello 0.61%. Il Dollar Index è in rialzo dello 0.18%, a 98.46 L'oro è sopra i 4700 dollari, con un aumento dello 0.63%. Il petrolio è in calo dello 0.71%, a 107 dollari. Il rendimento del decennale USA è in rialzo dell'1.2%, al 4.46%. I BTP 10Y sono stabili al 3.39%.

L'inflazione negli Stati Uniti è salita al 3.8%, spinta dai prezzi del petrolio dopo le tensioni con l'Iran. Questo aumento potrebbe aumentare la pressione sulla Fed per un intervento.

Oggi saranno pubblicati i dati sull'inflazione CPI e Core CPI negli Stati Uniti. La pressione sulla Fed potrebbe aumentare in base ai dati odierni.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
  Bitcoin si mantiene sopra gli ottantamila dollari, con una variazione del +0,14%. I flussi ETF mostrano un afflusso di 27,2 milioni di dollari. 
  Questo movimento avviene in un contesto di attenzione verso l'economia statunitense. 
  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna lo 0,57%, arrivando a duemilatrecento dollari, mentre Solana cede lo 0,60%, a 95,03 dollari. 
  BNB invece registra un aumento significativo del 2,91%, quotato a 678,48 dollari. 
  L'indice Fear & Greed scende a 42, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita. Per approfondire, trovate gli articoli sulla nostra piattaforma nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.84%, Shanghai up 0.67%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed down 0.16%, the VIX fell 0.61%. The Dollar Index is up 0.18%, at 98.46 Gold is above $4,700, with an increase of 0.63%. Oil is down 0.71%, at $107 The 10-year US yield is up 1.2%, at 4.46%. The 10Y BTPs are stable at 3.39%. US inflation rose to 3.8%, driven by oil prices after tensions with Iran. This increase could increase pressure on the Fed to intervene. Today, CPI and Core CPI inflation data will be released in the United States. Pressure on the Fed could increase based on today's data. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above eighty thousand dollars, with a variation of +0.14%. ETF flows show an inflow of $27.2 million. This movement occurs in a context of attention towards the US economy. Among altcoins, Ethereum gains 0.57%, reaching $2,300, while Solana drops 0.6%, to $95.03 BNB instead records a significant increase of 2.91%, quoted at $678.48 The Fear & Greed index falls to 42, in Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors. We are waiting for economic data to be released. For more details, find the articles on our platform in the Top Stories section. Thank you for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Does OPEC Still Matter?
articles.snippet: On April 28, the United Arab Emirates announced that it would leave OPEC, effective May 1 — ending nearly six decades as an OPEC member. In terms of oil production, it is the most significant country to leave the group. While multiple factors drove the decision to leave, the timing is notable — as the war with Iran has led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and focused global attention on oil prices. We asked four experts to consider the impact on OPEC’s future.Read more below. Kristian Coates Ulrichsen Fellow for the Middle East at the Baker Institute The post Does OPEC Still Matter? appeared first on War on the Rocks .
articles.summary_it: L'OPEC potrebbe perdere influenza a causa della decisione degli Emirati Arabi Uniti di lasciare l'organizzazione.
articles.summary_en: OPEC's influence may be waning due to the UAE's decision to leave the organization.

articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown discuss their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing stockpiles, subsidies, and trade restrictions,…

articles.title: Trump’s treatment of US allies has weakened his negotiating position with Xi
articles.snippet: Trump’s treatment of US allies has weakened his negotiating position with Xi Expert comment jon.wallace 12 May 2026 The president has alienated partners that once acted as force multipliers. But there are still opportunities to create a united front on common points of tension with Beijing. President Donald Trump travels to Beijing this week with the US’s alliance structure under enormous strain. Washington has fewer partners at its side, and a weaker hand to play. It doesn’t have to be this way. Alone, the US has leverage against Beijing, through controlling access to its advanced chips, sanctions on Chinese purchases of Iranian oil, and a consumer market Beijing can’t ignore. But Washington’s allies and partners provided strength that China has struggled to compete with – acting as force

articles.title: The Other Border Problem: How Russia and China’s Lawfare Threaten the Arctic
articles.snippet: What happens when the Arctic starts to look like the South China Sea?Historically, a neutral region where cooperation prevailed, the Arctic is quickly becoming a contested space. This is no more evident than in the increasing scope and volume of Russian and Chinese lawfare affecting the region. articles.title: Europe’s Gas Industry Seeks Relief From Storage Mandates
articles.snippet: European Union gas industry lobby groups are urging Brussels to relax gas storage refill targets amid the supply crunch prompted by the war in the Middle East. The EU has a refill target of 90% of storage capacity by November every year in a bid to secure sufficient supply for peak demand season in winter. The war, however, has removed a solid portion of global LNG supply, making the refilling job harder and more expensive. articles.title: Canada’s Economy Caught Between Oil Windfalls and Trade Wars
articles.snippet: A recent Bank of Canada Market Participants Survey has flagged geopolitical and trade tensions as the biggest risks facing the Canadian economy. Leading the downside are geopolitical risks led by the Middle East war, with 82% of respondents identifying it as the biggest risk, while 79% and 57% of respondents picked growing trade tensions and tightening global financial conditions, respectively. The shift from trade tensions dominating headline risks to Canada’s economy amid Trump tariffs is largely attributed to the Iran war, which has disrupted…
